transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Acme Head of ML), Sana Ahmed (Acme Infra), Mike Rivera (Acme SRE), Tina Lo (Acme Product)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes on this slot, we'll try to cover success criteria, what you're trying to measure, and then go into the harness integration stuff. sound good?
[00:12] Jordan Miles: yeah that's great. thanks Alex. quick context, we're building a real-time recommendations feature for our mobile app, so low latency is really important, but so is cost since we'll be doing millions of requests a day.
[00:25] Priya Patel: got it. curious, Jordan, what's your current stack and how are you running inference today?
[00:30] Jordan Miles: currently we have a microservice on EKS that calls a third-party API, we're using a smaller open model right now and some caching in front. but the kv cache isn't ideal, and concurrency spikes during promotions have been killing latency.
[00:45] Sana Ahmed: yeah and from infra side we can't overprovision, so we need predictable throughput. also we have SSO via Okta and corporate VPC requirements.
[00:55] Diego Ramos: understood. for the POC we usually do two parallel tracks: functional correctness/quality and performance. here it sounds like perf is the gating factor. correct?
[01:05] Jordan Miles: perf and cost per token. we want to know if Redwood can meet our 99th percentile SLO and beat the cost per inference we're paying now.
[01:15] Alex Chen: perfect - typical. for benchmarks we recommend we run your actual request scripts through our harness so results are realistic. we'll also test streaming endpoints vs non-streaming to see the tradeoffs for your workflow.
[01:26] Mike Rivera: on streaming vs non-streaming, can you clarify differences in how you measure throughput and what metrics we should expect?
[01:33] Priya Patel: sure. streaming splits response chunks over time and has steady token-rate latency characteristics; it can reduce time-to-first-token which matters for UX. non-streaming returns full payloads which can be more CPU/memory heavy and can have higher tail latency for long generations. in the harness we measure TTF token, TTF first byte, 50/95/99 percentiles, and end-to-end CPU/GPU utilization.
[01:50] Jordan Miles: what about KV cache and batching - we use prefix caching a lot. will that be part of the benchmark?
[01:58] Priya Patel: yes. we can emulate KV cache usage patterns. we have config options in the harness to replay prefix cache hits and misses, and to control batching windows so we can measure cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[02:10] Tina Lo: for success criteria, we want 99p latency < 400ms for streaming path at our baseline concurrency of 1k concurrent mobile sessions, and average cost per 1k tokens less than $0.20, roughly. is that doable to test in a week?
[02:26] Alex Chen: timeline seems tight but possible. we'll need your traces and scripts ASAP to create a representative workload. realistic baseline run typically takes 24-48 hours to provision and warm. we can aim for initial results in 4 business days once we have artifacts.
[02:40] Jordan Miles: OK, we'll provide traces. question: can you run the harness in our VPC or do you need to run in Redwood hosted environment?
[02:48] Diego Ramos: we support both. for secure POCs we can run a private harness in your VPC or a Redwood-hosted harness with VPC peering. private harness requires onboarding and some infra work but gives you more control over data egress.
[03:02] Sana Ahmed: security is non-negotiable - we'll need SOC2 docs, KMS integration details, and audit logs.
[03:08] Priya Patel: we'll share SOC2 and the KMS/HSM integration guide; audit logs are retained in the console and we can provide a sample export. we'll include that in the security packet.
[03:18] Jordan Miles: great. on the harness itself - our scripts are in Python and we use a custom batching layer in front of the client. can we just point the harness at our script or do we need to rewrite it?
[03:27] Alex Chen: usually customers provide a small wrapper around their clients. we can accept Python scripts and a short adapter; our harness repo has examples. ideally you drop in a script that reads from your trace file and emits requests the same way you do in prod.
[03:40] Mike Rivera: what's the expected load generation capability? we might want to simulate bursts up to 3k concurrent sessions for promotions.
[03:47] Priya Patel: the harness supports ramp profiles, constant load, and bursts. we'll provision load generators across zones to hit target concurrent sessions; for 3k concurrent we'll need to scale test infra and possibly use Dedicated capacity depending on model size.
[03:58] Jordan Miles: model size - we're looking at a 7B quantized model for the POC. how does quantization affect performance in your runtime?
[04:06] Priya Patel: quantized models reduce GPU memory and can drastically reduce cost with similar latency; our runtime has quantization-friendly execution paths. we'll include model variants in the test matrix: fp16, int8 quant, and the Redwood-verified optimized 7B.
[04:20] Tina Lo: will you measure cost modeling? we need a predicted monthly cost at our QPS and token mix.
[04:26] Alex Chen: yes - part of the benchmark deliverable is a cost projection: unit cost per 1M tokens for each config, and a rollout plan that balances cost/latency. we'll produce a small spreadsheet with estimated monthly spend under your traffic profile.
[04:38] Jordan Miles: nice. any gotchas for streaming tests? we're worried about connection churn from mobile clients.
[04:44] Diego Ramos: we'll emulate short-lived connections and intermittent connectivity. streaming tests will include time-to-first-byte and reconnect scenarios; we also measure token backpressure behavior so we'll see how pauses affect latency and cost.
[04:58] Sana Ahmed: network-wise we'll need to open certain ports for the load generators if you run from outside our VPC. I'll coordinate with Mike on IP allowlists.
[05:05] Mike Rivera: yes, I'll send the list. also question on observability - can we get token-level logs and per-request timing?
[05:12] Priya Patel: the Redwood console can export per-request timing and breakdowns (decode time, kernel time, batching delays). for POCs we can share CSV exports and dashboards.
[05:22] Jordan Miles: good. what's the typical acceptance criteria beyond raw latency/cost? like model quality regressions?
[05:28] Alex Chen: we recommend a small quality eval set - a holdout of prompts that represent failure modes. acceptance is: performance meets SLO, cost targets are within agreed band, and no significant quality regression on the eval set (we'll run automated comparisons).
[05:42] Tina Lo: ok. let's talk timelines and concrete next steps.
[05:46] Alex Chen: action items - we'll post the harness repo (link in notes), you provide traces and scripts, Priya will prepare test configs including streaming and non-streaming, and we'll schedule baseline runs. initial run results within 4 business days after artifacts.
[06:00] Jordan Miles: can you also include a canary plan - like if we move to Dedicated capacity later, what's the path?
[06:07] Diego Ramos: yes; we'll include a suggested rollout: start hosted for speed, then Dedicated reserved capacity for peak windows and finally private for compliance if needed. we'll sketch out autoscaling and fallback policies.
[06:18] Mike Rivera: any security checklist for the private harness? like SAML setup and KMS policies?
[06:23] Priya Patel: we'll include an onboarding checklist: Okta SAML config, service account keys, KMS key usage policy, IP allowlists, and audit log export steps.
[06:34] Jordan Miles: estimate of cost to run these benchmarks? we want to know test infra costs and Redwood charges if any.
[06:40] Alex Chen: we generally absorb small POC harness runs for proof points; large-scale runs may incur a test-infra pass-through. we'll flag that before running.
[06:48] Tina Lo: sounds fair. are there any known incompatibilities with our custom batching layer?
[06:53] Priya Patel: not usually - we can instrument a shim adapter. sometimes proprietary tokenization or special pre/post processing needs slight changes. we'll validate quickly once we see your script.
[07:05] Jordan Miles: ok, I think that's everything. thanks - really like the plan.
[07:09] Alex Chen: great. recap of immediate next steps: Alex to share harness repo + quickstart, Jordan to send traces + scripts, Priya to prepare test config, Mike to confirm network/IPs. we'll tentatively schedule the baseline run for Nov 24.
[07:25] Jordan Miles: confirmed. thanks everyone.

Notes: some transcription artifacts present - names occasionally abbreviated; technical terms sometimes hyphenated (K-V cache).
